items.headline: Kittle on the PUP list after the Achilles; Week 1 is not guaranteed
items.summary: George Kittle was placed on the PUP list while recovering from the torn Achilles suffered in the 2025 playoffs. He has said he wants to play Week 1, but there is no guarantee he comes off PUP in time. Jake Tonges and Luke Farrell would split tight end.

items.headline: Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List — out indefinitely
items.summary: Jacobs was placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List on 30 August and will open the regular season on it: he is paid and may be at the facility for meetings and treatment, but cannot practise or play until the league lifts it. His first court date is 17 November, and the league does not have to wait for the legal process to act. There is no return date.

items.headline: Tyreek Hill is a free agent, coming off a dislocated knee — may not play in 2026
items.summary: Miami released Tyreek Hill in February and his agent says he is not expected to sign anywhere before the season starts. He is recovering from a dislocated left knee with multiple torn ligaments including the ACL, suffered in September 2025. He may not be ready until mid-season, and there is no guarantee he plays at all in 2026. Consensus has him around WR98. Since 1995 only three receivers have torn an ACL at 30 or older and gone on to a 750-yard season; he turned 32 in March and his game is built on top-end speed.

items.headline: Trevor Etienne to IR with an ankle: eligible in Week 5, and he is not Travis
items.summary: Carolina placed Trevor Etienne on injured reserve with a designation to return after he hurt an ankle in Friday's preseason finale against Houston. He misses at least four games and is eligible in Week 5. He was the depth behind Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) and Jonathan Brooks, so AJ Dillon moves up. Trevor is not Travis Etienne, who starts for New Orleans — same surname, different player, different team.

items.headline: Green Bay's backfield has no established workload behind Jacobs
items.summary: MarShawn Lloyd is the projected starter with six career carries for 15 yards, having played one of a possible 34 games through injuries. Chris Brooks (395 career rushing yards at 4.8 a carry) is the third-down back, and Green Bay traded for Kaleb Johnson, who ran 28 times for 69 yards as a Pittsburgh rookie. Treat any projection here as a positional average wearing a name: none of the three has the sample to earn one.

items.headline: Jeremiyah Love has a high-ankle sprain; his coach says he is progressing toward Week 1
items.summary: The No. 3 pick hurt the ankle on his final touch of his preseason debut and Schefter reported a high-ankle sprain on 16 August. He has been limited to individual work for two weeks. On 31 August Mike LaFleur said he is 'confident that he's progressing well' and that Love 'took another step'. The team hopes for the 13 September opener against the Chargers; a high-ankle sprain typically runs four to six weeks, so Week 1 sits at the early edge. Tyler Allgeier opens if he cannot go, with Conner on IR.

items.headline: The market has already repriced Green Bay: Jacobs fell from 36th to 87th in ESPN's mock, Lloyd rose to 70th
items.summary: In ESPN's 12-team PPR mock draft held after the exempt-list news, Josh Jacobs — 36th overall the week before — went 87th, the 33rd running back taken. MarShawn Lloyd went 70th (RB26) after being RB40 in the previous mock. FantasyPros' ADP tracker had Lloyd up 16 spots in a week before the news broke. Expect the same in any draft this week: Jacobs is a stash, not a starter, and Lloyd will not last past the sixth round.

items.headline: Keenan Allen signed with the Colts on 19 August; Alec Pierce came off PUP on the 27th with no second procedure
items.summary: Allen signed a one-year, $8.32 million deal with Indianapolis on 19 August, reuniting with Shane Steichen. He has run most of his career from the slot, where Josh Downs runs 81% of his routes, so Downs is the one squeezed. An earlier report that Pierce had a second ankle procedure is wrong per GM Chris Ballard: a PRP injection in January, surgery in March, and he was activated from PUP on 27 August with two-plus weeks of practice before the 13 September opener.

items.headline: Rashee Rice is not suspended to open 2026: the league closed its review with no discipline
items.summary: After a 30-day jail sentence for a positive THC test, the NFL will not suspend Rice under the personal conduct policy — the league no longer suspends for marijuana. He is available from Week 1 with no discipline pending, which matters because he sits WR8 in Mike Clay's 31 August rankings and the draft market had priced in risk.

items.headline: Where the market and this board disagree most, from eight ranking sources dated 29-31 August
items.summary: Median overall PPR rank across PFN, SI (Fabiano), RotoWire consensus, CBS/SportsLine, WalterFootball, PFF, Yahoo consensus and ESPN (Mike Clay, positional) against this board. The market takes these earlier than the board does, so you cannot wait on them: Omarion Hampton (market 12, board 55 — six weighted games of history, so 64% of his number is the positional prior), Saquon Barkley (13 vs 30 — age factor 0.78 at 29), Ashton Jeanty (14 vs 32 — 51% prior after an injured rookie year), Derrick Henry (14 vs 136 — age factor 0.61 at 32, the curve's most aggressive point), Colston Loveland (32 vs 119 — 50% prior) and Emeka Egbuka (36 vs 96 — 51% prior). The board is higher than the market on Puka Nacua (1 vs 4), Trey McBride (7 vs 21, tight-end scarcity), De'Von Achane (6 vs 10) and Josh Allen (15 vs 40 — the market waits on quarterbacks; a 12-team single-QB VOR does not). None of this changes a number: the model is walk-forward validated and the age curve improved running-back error most of all, but at 32 it is an extrapolation and the market says so.
